name: Allopurinol
route_note: oral tablet once daily, titrated to serum urate target; IV for tumour lysis prevention

discovery.by: Roland Robins (synthesis); Gertrude Elion and George Hitchings, Burroughs Wellcome (development)
discovery.note: Studied first as an adjunct to raise mercaptopurine levels in leukaemia, then found to lower uric acid.

tagline: The mainstay of gout prevention, from Nobel laureates Elion and Hitchings
summary: Allopurinol is a purine analogue that inhibits xanthine oxidase and so lowers production of uric acid. It is the first-line urate-lowering therapy for chronic gout and is used to prevent tumour lysis syndrome; serious skin reactions are strongly associated with the HLA-B*58:01 allele.
mechanism: Xanthine oxidase catalyses the last two steps of purine breakdown, hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. Allopurinol, a structural isomer of hypoxanthine, and its long-lived active metabolite oxypurinol (alloxanthine) inhibit the enzyme.

Uric acid levels fall, urate crystals in joints and tissues slowly dissolve, and gout flares and tophi diminish over months; the more soluble precursors hypoxanthine and xanthine are excreted instead. Starting treatment can trigger flares, so prophylaxis such as colchicine is often given.
uses: Chronic gout and hyperuricaemia with tophi or recurrent flares
Prevention of tumour lysis syndrome during chemotherapy
Recurrent calcium oxalate kidney stones with hyperuricosuria

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Roland Robins synthesises allopurinol; Elion and Hitchings study it at Burroughs Wellcome.

history.title: Gout trials
history.detail: Clinical studies show allopurinol lowers uric acid in gout.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Elion and Hitchings (with James Black) receive the Nobel Prize for principles of drug treatment, including allopurinol.

history.title: HLA-B*5801 link
history.detail: Researchers in Taiwan report that HLA-B*58:01 is strongly associated with allopurinol-induced SJS/TEN (PNAS 2005).

history.title: ACR guideline
history.detail: The American College of Rheumatology recommends allopurinol as first-line urate-lowering therapy with HLA-B*58:01 testing in high-risk ancestry groups.

history.title: ALL-HEART
history.detail: The ALL-HEART trial finds allopurinol does not reduce cardiovascular events in ischaemic heart disease without gout.

serious: bone marrow suppression with azathioprine or mercaptopurine

facts: Allopurinol greatly increases azathioprine and mercaptopurine toxicity, since both are inactivated by xanthine oxidase.
HLA-B*58:01 is common in Han Chinese, Korean and Thai populations, in whom pre-treatment testing is often recommended.

references.title: Hung SI et al. HLA-B*5801 and allopurinol-induced severe cutaneous reactions (PNAS 2005)
